nodes.summary: James–Stein (1961): for `p ≥ 3` and `X ~ N(θ, I_p)`, `‖X‖⁻²` is integrable and the risk of the James–Stein estimator is `p - (p - 2)² E[‖X‖⁻²]`.
nodes.title: James–Stein

nodes.summary: For `X ~ N(μ, v)` and an everywhere differentiable `g` with integrable derivative, `(X - μ) g(X)` is integrable and `E[(X - μ) g(X)] = v E[g'(X)]`. For `v = 0` both sides vanish.
nodes.title: Stein's lemma

nodes.summary: James–Stein dominance (Stein 1956, James–Stein 1961): for `p ≥ 3`, the James–Stein estimator has strictly smaller quadratic risk than `X` at every mean `θ`.
nodes.title: James–Stein dominance

nodes.summary: Stein's lemma, coordinate form: for `X ~ N(θ, I_p)` and a function `h` whose slices along the `i`-th axis are differentiable everywhere (for almost every base point) with integrable partial derivative `dh`, `E[(Xᵢ - θᵢ) h(X)] = E[dh(X)]` whenever `(Xᵢ - θᵢ) h(X)` is integrable. Unlike the one-dimensional case, this integrability does not follow from that of `dh`: `h(x) = exp(x₁²)` has `∂₀ h = 0` but `x₀ h(x)` is…
nodes.title: Stein's lemma

nodes.summary: For `X ~ N(θ, I_p)` and an estimator `X + g(X)` whose coordinates `gᵢ` are square integrable and satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma in the `i`-th coordinate with partial derivative `dgᵢ`, the quadratic risk is `p + E[∑ gᵢ(X)² + 2 ∑ dgᵢ(X)]`.
nodes.title: Stein's unbiased risk estimate

nodes.summary: The quadratic risk of the usual estimator `X` of the mean of `N(θ, I_p)` is `p`.
nodes.title: Quadratic risk of the usual Gaussian mean estimator

nodes.summary: The James–Stein estimator `δ(x) = (1 - (p - 2) / ‖x‖²) x` of the mean of `N(θ, I_p)`. At `x = 0` the factor is `1` by Lean's `a / 0 = 0` convention, so `δ(0) = 0`.
nodes.title: James–Stein estimator
